cohort: The study included 61 patients with non-cephalic fetuses, 79% of whom agreed to undergo an ECV trial, out of 1332 total deliveries at a single perinatal center.
finding: ECV performed under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia demonstrated significant medical cost savings and a reduction in the cesarean rate, with a high success rate and without significant adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: ECV adoption reduced the cesarean rate from 26.7% to 23.9% by facilitating normal vaginal deliveries, leading to medical cost savings.
